{{ Cross-country skiing at the 2026 Winter Olympics}}

The '''women's 20 kilometre skiathlon''' competition in [[Cross-country skiing at the 2026 Winter Olympics|cross-country skiing]] at the [[2026 Winter Olympics]] was held on 7 February,<!-- 2026--> at the [[Cross country and biathlon center Fabio Canal]] in [[Tesero]].<ref name=schedule>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/schedule/ccs|title=2026 Olympic Winter Games Competition Schedule Version - Cross-country skiing|access-date=1 February 2026}}</ref> [[Frida Karlsson]] of Sweden won the race, and her teammate [[Ebba Andersson (cross-country skier)|Ebba Andersson]] finished second. [[Heidi Weng]] of Norway won the bronze medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/winter/cross-country-skiing/sweden-frida-karlsson-wins-gold-in-skiathlon-9.7078962|title=Sweden's Frida Karlsson wins Olympic gold in skiathlon|publisher=CBC|accessdate=28 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/frida-karlsson-wins-gold-skiathlon-jessie-diggins-caught-lap-mishap|title=Frida Karlsson wins gold in skiathlon, Jessie Diggins caught in lap mishap|publisher=NBC Olympics|accessdate=28 February 2026}}</ref> For Karlsson, it was the first individual Olympic medal and the first gold (after a team bronze in 2022). It was also the first individual Olympic medal for Andersson.

==Background==
At the previous Olympics, the women's skiathlon was 15 km; it was extended to 20 km for the 2026 Winter Olympics by FIS to match men's and women's event distances. The 2022 champion, [[Therese Johaug]], retired from competitions,<ref>{{cite news |title=Ski great Therese Johaug puts family first and ends career before 2026 Winter Olympics |url=https://apnews.com/article/therese-johaug-retires-2026-olympics-skiing-9c89754f9c9900633d2a34ad0fecc1ba |access-date=26 May 2025 |work=AP News}}</ref> the silver medalist [[Natalya Nepryayeva]] took a maternity leave and effectively stopped competing, while the bronze medalist, [[Teresa Stadlober]], qualified for the event. [[Jessie Diggins]] was leading both overall and distance standings of the [[2025–26 FIS Cross-Country World Cup|FIS Cross-Country World Cup]] before the Olympics. [[Ebba Andersson (cross-country skier)|Ebba Andersson]] was the [[FIS Nordic World Ski Championships 2025 – Women's 20 kilometre skiathlon|2025 world champion]] in the event.
